title: The hour has come (John 17:1–5)
hookLine: he lifts his eyes and prays for the Father's glory

cards: For three chapters Jesus has been talking to his friends. Now, suddenly, he stops talking to them and starts talking to God, out loud, while they listen. The prayer fills the whole of John seventeen.

Christians often call it the High Priestly Prayer, because in it he stands between God and his friends, the way a priest does. And it starts with a small detail John doesn't want you to miss. He looks up.

teach.h: HE LIFTS HIS EYES, AS AT LAZARUS'S TOMB.
teach.b: In the King James Bible: "These words spake Jesus, and lifted up his eyes to heaven, and said, Father, the hour is come; glorify thy Son, that thy Son also may glorify thee."
John has shown this before: at Lazarus's tomb, too, Jesus lifted up his eyes and said, Father.

teach.h: NOT YET, NOT YET, AND NOW THE HOUR.
teach.b: Then: the hour is come. If you've read John from the start, that lands hard. At the wedding at Cana, Jesus told his mother, "mine hour is not yet come."
More than once, people tried to seize him and couldn't, John says, because his hour had not yet come. Then, when some Greeks came looking for him, he said it at last: the hour is come.
The whole Gospel has been counting down to this. And the hour is for glory. In John, that word does something unexpected.
The glory isn't a throne or a crown.

teach.h: IN JOHN, THE GLORY IS THE CROSS.
teach.b: In John's telling it is bound up with the cross: the moment that looks like shame is the moment John calls glory.
Then a definition, the line in today's carry: "And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent."
It doesn't define eternal life as living forever, or as a place you go after you die.
It defines it as knowing. And knowing, in the Bible, is often close and personal: the way you know a friend, not a fact. So for John, eternal life can begin now, in a relationship, not only later.

how: Many churches read John 17 in the days between Ascension and Pentecost, and some Christians pray standing with eyes and hands lifted.

a fixed time of daily prayer in the temple

"These words spake Jesus, and lifted up his eyes to heaven, and said, Father, the hour is come."
in John 17:3, eternal life is defined as living forever
it's defined as knowing: "that they might know thee the only true God."
at Cana, Jesus said his hour had already come
he said, "mine hour is not yet come." the hour arrives near the end of the Gospel.

games.q: you've talked to your friends for hours. now it's time to pray, out loud, in front of them. how do you begin?
o: kneel and bow your head in silence.
lift your eyes to heaven and say: Father, the hour is come.
ask them to pray for you first.
games.why: "These words spake Jesus, and lifted up his eyes to heaven, and said, Father, the hour is come."

practice: Sit straight, or stand, and slowly lift your face toward the ceiling or a window's sky, noticing how different it feels from looking down at a screen.
If you pray, pray there with your eyes lifted, even just the word Father; if not, let your eyes rest on something high and wide, and let your thoughts grow bigger than the day so far.

wordCard.voice: Hora. John's word for the hour, the moment the whole Gospel has been counting toward: the cross, which John calls glory.

orig.note: Greek: the hour has come. hora, the hour, is John's word for the time of the cross.

carryVoice: Your line: this is life eternal. Knowing, not just lasting, and it can start now. See you tomorrow.
